52576-a-manual-of-american-literature.description: A book by G. P. Putnam’S Sons. by rendering English literature as universally known as possible beyond the limits of the British Empire.” In another place, Baron Tauchnitz describes “the mission” of his Collection to be the “spreading and strengthening the love for English literature outside of England and her Colonies.”

8728-the-winning-of-canada-a-chronicle-o.title: The Winning Of Canada A Chronicle Of Wolfe
8728-the-winning-of-canada-a-chronicle-o.creator: William Wood
8728-the-winning-of-canada-a-chronicle-o.description: A book by William Wood. The Wolfes are of an old and honourable line. Many hundreds of years ago their forefathers lived in England and later on in Wales. Later still, in the fifteenth century, before America was discovered, they were living in Ireland.

arxiv-1412-7240.title: Effects of Shock Waves on Neutrino Oscillations in Three Supernova Models
arxiv-1412-7240.creator: Jing Xu 1 , Li-Jun Hu 1 , Rui-Cheng Li 1 , Xin-Heng Guo 1 and Bing-Lin Young 2,3
arxiv-1412-7240.description: Abstract It has been realized that the shock wave effects play an important role in neutrino oscillations during the supernova explosion. In recent years, with the development of simulations about supernova explosion, we have a better understanding about the density profiles and the shock waves in supernovae than before.

arxiv-1608-06192.title: Efficient Continuous Relaxations for Dense CRF
arxiv-1608-06192.creator: Alban Desmaison 1, Rudy Bunel 1, Pushmeet Kohli 2, Philip H.S. Torr 1, M. Pawan Kumar 1
arxiv-1608-06192.description: Abstract Dense conditional random fields (CRF) with Gaussian pairwise potentials have emerged as a popular framework for several computer vision applications such as stereo correspondence and semantic segmentation. By modeling long-range interactions, dense CRFs provide a more detailed labelling compared to their sparse counterparts.

arxiv-2012-14081.title: Objective Bayesian analysis for the differential entropy of the Gamma distribution
arxiv-2012-14081.creator: Eduardo Ramos, Osafu A. Egbon, Pedro L. Ramos, Francisco A. Rodrigues, Francisco Louzada
arxiv-2012-14081.description: Abstract Summary The present paper introduces a fully objective Bayesian analysis to obtain the posterior distribution of an entropy measure. Notably, we consider the gamma distribution, which describes many natural phenomena in physics, engineering, and biology. We reparametrize the model in terms of entropy, and different objective priors are derived, such as Jeffreys prior, reference prior, and matching priors.

arxiv-2109-08320.title: Adding the Relation Meets to the Temporal Logic of Prefixes and Infixes Makes It EXPSPACE-Complete
arxiv-2109-08320.creator: Laura Bozzelli, Angelo Montanari, Adriano Peron, Pietro Sala
arxiv-2109-08320.description: Abstract The choice of the right trade-off between expressiveness and complexity is the main issue in interval temporal logic. In their seminal paper [ 11 ] , Halpern and Shoham showed that the satisfiability problem for 𝖧𝖲 \mathsf{HS} (the temporal logic of Allen’s relations) is highly undecidable over any reasonable class of linear orders.

arxiv-2112-10840.title: Anomalous Residual Surface Conductivity in a Superconductor with Strong Spin-Orbit Coupling
arxiv-2112-10840.creator: J. R. Chamorro, P. Chauhan, C. Sun, N. Varnava, M. J. Winiarski, N. Ng, H. K. Vivanco, L. A. Pressley, C. M. Pasco, D. Vanderbilt, Yi Li, N. P. Armitage, T. M. McQueen
arxiv-2112-10840.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. R. Chamorro, P. Chauhan, C. Sun, N. Varnava, M. J. Winiarski, N. Ng, H. K. Vivanco, L. A. Pressley, C. M. Pasco, D. Vanderbilt, Yi Li, N. P. Armitage, T. M. McQueen. Conventional BCS superconductors are expected to exhibit a conductivity with vanishing dissipation with decreasing temperature.

arxiv-2210-14364.title: Functional Simulation of Real-Time Quantum Control Software
arxiv-2210-14364.creator: Leon Riesebos, Kenneth R. Brown
arxiv-2210-14364.description: Abstract Modern quantum computers rely heavily on real-time control systems for operation. Software for these systems is becoming increasingly more complex due to the demand for more features and more real-time devices to control. Unfortunately, testing real-time control software is often a complex process, and existing simulation software is not usable or practical for software testing.

arxiv-2304-08705.title: The chain control set of discrete-time linear systems on the affine two-dimensional Lie group Journal: Journal of Dinamical and Control Systems
arxiv-2304-08705.creator: Thiago Matheus Cavalheiro, João Augusto Navarro Cossich, Alexandre José Santana
arxiv-2304-08705.description: Abstract In this paper, we present conditions for the existence and uniqueness of chain control sets of discrete-time linear systems on the affine two-dimensional Lie group. More specifically, we prove that these chain control sets are given by the union of an infinite number of control sets with empty interiors.

arxiv-2306-04347.title: World Models for Math Story Problems
arxiv-2306-04347.creator: Andreas Opedal Niklas Stoehr Abulhair Saparov Mrinmaya Sachan
arxiv-2306-04347.description: Abstract Solving math story problems is a complex task for students and NLP models alike, requiring them to understand the world as described in the story and reason over it to compute an answer. Recent years have seen impressive performance on automatically solving these problems with large pre-trained language models and innovative techniques to prompt them.

arxiv-2311-02046.title: Correlations of Conserved Quantities at Finite Baryon Density
arxiv-2311-02046.creator: Oleh Savchuk, Scott Pratt
arxiv-2311-02046.description: Abstract Correlations involving the seven conserved quantities, namely energy, baryon number, electric charge, strangeness, and the three components of momentum, give rise to correlations in heavy-ion collisions. Through the utilization of a simple one-dimensional hydrodynamic model, we calculate the evolution of the entire 7 × 7 7\times 7 matrix of correlations as a function of relative spatial rapidity.

arxiv-2402-12880.title: Autism Detection in Speech – A Survey
arxiv-2402-12880.creator: Nadine Probol, Margot Mieskes
arxiv-2402-12880.description: Abstract There has been a range of studies of how autism is displayed in voice, speech, and language. We analyse studies from the biomedical, as well as the psychological domain, but also from the NLP domain in order to find linguistic, prosodic and acoustic cues that could indicate autism. Our survey looks at all three domains.

arxiv-2402-14532.title: A Framework for Variational Inference of Lightweight Bayesian Neural Networks with Heteroscedastic Uncertainties
arxiv-2402-14532.creator: David J. Schodt, Ryan Brown, Michael Merritt, Samuel Park, Delsin Menolascino, Mark A. Peot
arxiv-2402-14532.description: Abstract Obtaining heteroscedastic predictive uncertainties from a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) is vital to many applications. Often, heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainties are learned as outputs of the BNN in addition to the predictive means, however doing so may necessitate adding more learnable parameters to the network.

arxiv-2403-07054.title: Minimal Fractional Topological Insulator in half-filled conjugate moiré Chern bands
arxiv-2403-07054.creator: Chao-Ming Jian, Meng Cheng, Cenke Xu
arxiv-2403-07054.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chao-Ming Jian, Meng Cheng, Cenke Xu. We propose a “minimal” fractional topological insulator (mFTI), motivated by the recent experimental report on the signatures of FTI at total filling factor ν tot = 3 \nu_{\rm tot}=3 in a transition metal dichalcogenide moiré system.

arxiv-2404-15018.title: Conformal Predictive Systems Under Covariate Shift
arxiv-2404-15018.creator: Jef Jonkers, Glenn Van Wallendael, Luc Duchateau, Sofie Van Hoecke
arxiv-2404-15018.description: Abstract Conformal predictive systems (CPS) offer a versatile framework for constructing predictive distributions, allowing for calibrated inference and informative decision-making. However, their applicability has been limited to scenarios adhering to the independent and identically distributed (IID) model assumption. This paper extends CPS to accommodate scenarios characterized by covariate shifts.

arxiv-2405-19518.title: Prediction Beyond the Medium Range with an Atmosphere-Ocean Model that Combines Physics-based Modeling and Machine Learning Thanks: Currently at the University of Chicago
arxiv-2405-19518.description: Abstract This paper explores the potential of a hybrid modeling approach that combines machine learning (ML) with conventional physics-based modeling for weather prediction beyond the medium range. It extends the work of Arcomano et al. (2022) , which tested the approach for short- and medium-range weather prediction, and the work of Arcomano et al.

arxiv-2407-03883.title: Protecting Deep Learning Model Copyrights with Adversarial Example-Free Reuse Detection
arxiv-2407-03883.creator: Xiaokun Luan 1 , Xiyue Zhang 2 , Jingyi Wang 3 , Meng Sun 1 §
arxiv-2407-03883.description: Abstract Model reuse techniques can reduce the resource requirements for training high-performance deep neural networks (DNNs) by leveraging existing models. However, unauthorized reuse and replication of DNNs can lead to copyright infringement and economic loss to the model owner. This underscores the need to analyze the reuse relation between DNNs and develop copyright protection techniques to safeguard intellectual property rights.

arxiv-2408-04489.creator: IN THE
arxiv-2408-04489.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by IN THE. arxiv-2503-08472.title: Optimizing Ride-Pooling Operations with Extended Pickup and Drop-Off Flexibility
arxiv-2503-08472.creator: Hao Jiang, Yixin Xu, Pradeep VARAKANTHAM
arxiv-2503-08472.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hao Jiang, Yixin Xu, Pradeep VARAKANTHAM. The Ride-Pool Matching Problem (RMP) is central to on-demand ride-pooling services, where vehicles must be matched with multiple requests while adhering to service constraints such as pickup delays, detour limits, and vehicle capacity. Most existing RMP solutions assume passengers are picked up and dropped off at their original locations, neglecting the potential for passengers to walk to nearby spots to meet vehicles. This assumption restricts the optimization potential in ride-pooling operations.

arxiv-2509-04430.title: Unveiling the Role of Data Uncertainty in Tabular Deep Learning
arxiv-2509-04430.creator: Nikolay Kartashev, Ivan Rubachev, Artem Babenko
arxiv-2509-04430.description: Abstract Recent advancements in tabular deep learning have demonstrated exceptional practical performance, yet the field often lacks a clear understanding of why these techniques actually succeed. To address this gap, our paper highlights the importance of the concept of data uncertainty for explaining the effectiveness of the recent tabular DL methods.

arxiv-2509-13896.title: Mind the Ethics! The Overlooked Ethical Dimensions of GenAI in Software Modeling Education
arxiv-2509-13896.creator: Shalini Chakraborty, Lola Burgueño, Nathalie Moreno, Javier Troya, Paula Muñoz
arxiv-2509-13896.description: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly gaining momentum in software modeling education, embraced by both students and educators. As GenAI assists with interpreting requirements, formalizing models, and translating students’ mental models into structured notations, it increasingly shapes core learning outcomes such as domain comprehension, diagrammatic thinking, and modeling fluency without clear ethical oversight or pedagogical guidelines.

arxiv-2603-01472.title: Two Lyman Continuum Escape Mechanisms at Play in z ∼ 0.3 z\sim 0.3 galaxies Revealed by Infrared Observations Journal: ApJL
arxiv-2603-01472.creator: Fang-Ting Yuan, Zhen-Ya Zheng, Chunyan Jiang, Shuairu Zhu

arxiv-2605-21537.title: Articulate but Wrong: Self-Review Failures in LLM-Based Code Modernization
arxiv-2605-21537.creator: Gokul Chandra Purnachandra Reddy, Aditya Lolla, Harsha Sanku

britannica-1911-florus-julius.title: Florus, Julius (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-florus-julius.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-florus-julius.description: Article 'Florus, Julius' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. His name has been immortalized by Horace, who dedicated to him two of his Epistles (i. 2), from which it would appear that he composed lyrics of a light, agreeable kind. The statement of Porphyrion, the old commentator on Horace, that Florus himself wrote satires, is probably erroneous, but he may have edited selections from the earlier satirists (Ennius, Lucilius, Varro).

pmc-10565201.title: Health and economic impacts of introducing specific excise tax to waterpipe tobacco in Egypt: a simulation model of simple and mixed tax policy approaches
pmc-10565201.creator: Aya Mostafa, Ali Chalak, Rima Nakkash, Ruba Abla, Yousef S Khader, Niveen ME Abu-Rmeileh, Ramzi G Salloum, Mohammed Jawad
pmc-10565201.description: IntroductionWaterpipe tobacco is taxed at half the rate of cigarettes in Egypt and, unlike cigarettes, does not have a specific excise component. We aimed to simulate the introduction of a specific excise tax on waterpipe tobacco consumption, premature deaths and government waterpipe tobacco revenue in Egypt.

pmc-11316749.title: OTUD6 deubiquitination of RPS7/eS7 on the free 40 S ribosome regulates global protein translation and stress
pmc-11316749.creator: Sammy Villa, Pankaj Dwivedi, Aaron Stahl, Trent Hinkle, Christopher M Rose, Donald S Kirkpatrick, Seth M Tomchik, Vishva M Dixit, Fred W Wolf
pmc-11316749.description: Ribosomes are regulated by evolutionarily conserved ubiquitination/deubiquitination events. We uncover the role of the deubiquitinase OTUD6 in regulating global protein translation through deubiquitination of the RPS7/eS7 subunit on the free 40 S ribosome in vivo in Drosophila. Coimmunoprecipitation and enrichment of monoubiquitinated proteins from catalytically inactive OTUD6 flies reveal RPS7 as the ribosomal substrate.

pmc-11337586.title: Building microbial consortia to enhance straw degradation, phosphorus solubilization, and soil fertility for rice growth
pmc-11337586.creator: Songhao Che, Yufeng Xu, Xueting Qin, Shiqi Tian, Jianing Wang, Xueying Zhou, Zhenning Cao, Dongchao Wang, Meikang Wu, Zhihai Wu, Meiying Yang, Lei Wu, Xue Yang
pmc-11337586.description: Straw pollution and the increasing scarcity of phosphorus resources in many regions of China have had severe impacts on the growing conditions for crop plants. Using microbial methods to enhance straw decomposition rate and phosphorus utilization offers effective solutions to address these problems.

pmc-11513821.title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae incidence, phenotype, and severity in children and adolescents in Denmark before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide multicentre population-based cohort study
pmc-11513821.creator: Kia H.S. Dungu, Mette Holm, Ulla Hartling, Lise H. Jensen, Allan Bybeck Nielsen, Lisbeth S. Schmidt, Lise B. Toustrup, Lotte H. Hansen, Kathrin W. Dahl, Kirstine T. Matthesen, Anne C. Nordholm, Søren Uldum, Hanne-Dorthe Emborg, Maren J.H. Rytter, Ulrikka Nygaard
pmc-11513821.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBackgroundMycoplasma pneumoniae infections resurged globally in 2023–2024 after a three-year decline during the COVID-19 pandemic. We explored the incidence and severity of M pneumoniae infections in children and adolescents before, during, and after the pandemic.MethodsThis nationwide, population-based cohort study included all Danish children and adolescents aged 0–17 years with a positive M pneumoniae PCR test from May 1, 2016, to April 30, 2024. We obtained clinical details for patients hospitalised for 24 h or more.

pmc-11531490.title: Novel optical optode for selective detection and removal of ultra-trace level of mercury ions in different environmental real samples
pmc-11531490.creator: Hager A. Dayra, Magdy Y. Abdelaal, Magdi E. Khalifa, A. B. Abdallah
pmc-11531490.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Owing to the high cost and unavailability of different analytical techniques, there is an urgent need to develop new techniques not only for detecting but also removing mercury ions in real samples. Thus, an optical chemical sensor based on the anchoring of phenanthraquinone monophenylthiosemicarbazone in a plasticized cellulose triacetate membrane was fabricated and applied to the recognition and removal of mercury ions from aqueous solutions. The synthesized optode was characterized by FT-IR, SEM, AFM, and thermal analysis.

pmc-11618766.creator: Mohsen Haghighat, Thomas Darcie, Levi Smith
pmc-11618766.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11960386.title: SPOUT1 variants associated with autosomal-recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
pmc-11960386.creator: Wenwei Liu, Kai Gao, Xilong Du, Sijia Wen, Huifang Yan, Jingmin Wang, Yong Wang, Conglei Song, Li Lin, Taoyun Ji, Weiyue Gu, Yuwu Jiang
pmc-11960386.description: BackgroundDevelopmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is a group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by early-onset seizures predominantly attributed to genetic causes. Nevertheless, numerous patients remain without identification of a genetic cause.MethodsWe present four unrelated Chinese patients with SPOUT1 compound heterozygous variants, all of whom were diagnosed with DEE. We also investigated functions of SPOUT1 using the spout1 knockout zebrafish model.

pmc-12740235.title: Non-uniform contextual interactions in the visual cortex place fundamental limits on spatial vision
pmc-12740235.creator: Mitchell P Morton, Sachira Denagamage, Nyomi V Hudson, Anirvan S Nandy
pmc-12740235.description: SUMMARYA common assumption is that contextual integration in the primary visual cortex (V1) is spatially uniform. However, perceptual phenomena such as visual crowding reveal non-uniform interactions, with flankers at specific geometries exerting stronger effects. To resolve this discrepancy, we investigated how flanker geometry impacted the representation of a target stimulus in the laminar microcircuits of V1.

pmc-13342157.title: Choosing the next option: a scenario-based roadmap for b/tsDMARD sequencing in rheumatoid arthritis
pmc-13342157.creator: Chamaida Plasencia-Rodríguez, Ana M. Ortiz, Loreto Carmona, Mercedes Guerra-Rodríguez, Petra Díaz del Campo, José M. Álvaro-Gracia
pmc-13342157.description: BackgroundBiologic (b) and targeted synthetic (ts) DMARDs have expanded rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment options, but evidence guiding sequencing after b/tsDMARD failure remains heterogeneous and difficult to translate into clinical practice.ObjectiveTo provide a pragmatic, scenario-based synthesis to guide next-therapy choice in RA after discontinuation of a b/tsDMARD.

pmc-13483854.title: Minimum acceptable diet and its associated factors among children aged 6-23months in rural households of South Ethiopia
pmc-13483854.creator: Kassahun Fikadu, Abinet Teshome, Zeleke Hailemariam
pmc-13483854.description: BackgroundOptimal nutrition throughout the first 1,000 days is critical for a child’s development, but malnutrition remains a major issue in Ethiopia. The Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) is an important indication of nutritional quality in children aged 6–23 months, although its prevalence and determinants vary significantly across the country.

pmc-13575243.title: Outcomes of patients with higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms treated with hypomethylating agents + venetoclax—an analysis from the International Consortium for MDS (icMDS) VALIDATE database
pmc-13575243.creator: Jan Philipp Bewersdorf, Tariq Kewan, Luca Lanino, Wei Wei, Tulika Rudra Gupta, Jessica M. Stempel, Najla H. Al Ali, Amy E. DeZern, Mikkael A. Sekeres, Geoffrey L. Uy, Samuel Urrutia, Hetty E. Carraway, Pinkal Desai, Elizabeth A. Griffiths, Eytan M. Stein, Andrew M. Brunner, Christine McMahon, Rory M
pmc-13575243.description: Monotherapy with hypomethylating agents (HMA) remains the standard of care for patients with higher-risk myelodysplastic neoplasms (HR-MDS). Recently, the randomized phase III VERONA study evaluating azacitidine plus venetoclax (VEN) versus azacitidine plus placebo in newly diagnosed HR-MDS showed no difference in overall survival (OS) between the two arms.

pmc-13628770.title: Elucidating the biochemical properties of limonene synthase from Agastache rugosa
pmc-13628770.creator: Sun-Yong Jung, Yeon-Ju Jeong, Min-Ju Seo, Jiyeun Yi, Bong Hyun Sung, Soo-Jin Yeom
pmc-13628770.description: BackgroundLimonene, a monocyclic monoterpene abundant in citrus essential oils, is extensively utilized in the fragrance, flavor, and pharmaceutical industries. Limonene synthase (LS) is a key enzyme in limonene biosynthesis by converting geranyl pyrophosphate to limonene. Despite its industrial significance, microbial limonene production is limited to a few LSs due to expression challenges.

pmc-13671097.title: Multidisciplinary Management of a Giant Ovarian Sertoli–Leydig Cell Tumor Presenting With Isosexual Precocious Puberty: A Pediatric Case Report
pmc-13671097.creator: Sanaa Bouramdane, Kenza Elmkaddem, Nawal Hammas, Meryem Boubbou, Othmane Alaoui, Khalid Khattala, Youssef Bouabdellah, Sarra Benmiloud
pmc-13671097.description: Sertoli–Leydig cell tumors (SLCTs) are rare ovarian sex cord‐stromal tumors, particularly uncommon in the pediatric population. They are typically androgen‐secreting, while estrogen‐secreting forms are rare and may lead to diagnostic confusion with granulosa cell tumors. We report the case of a 7‐year‐old girl presenting with progressive abdominal distension and isosexual precocious puberty.
